records.benchmarkId: ENERGIZE original randomized endpoint versus 2026 open-label hemoglobin durability evidence
records.benchmarkContext: Randomized 24-week ENERGIZE NCT04770753 produced hemoglobin response 55/130 (42%) mitapivat versus 1/64 (2%) placebo, 41 percentage point adjusted difference, 95% CI 32–50. Later open-label extension is a distinct post-hoc, uncontrolled and selected survivor cohort, not an independent pivotal replicate.
records.observedResult: Conference abstract O33 with exact NCT04770753: 182 entered OLE, 121 continuing mitapivat, 61 crossover; among 55 original randomized responders mean Hb response duration 17.9 (SD3.6) weeks within double-blind period versus 43.6 (SD24.2) weeks cumulatively through OLE. Seventy-two of 121 (59.5%) originally active-treated achieved an OLE Hb response and some lasted up to 93.3 weeks.
records.uncertaintyReview: OLE lacked placebo comparator, enrollment selected DB completers, includes post-hoc responder classification, different follow-up exposure (median 71 weeks active-active vs 44 weeks placebo-active) and potential informative dropout. Longer period is encouraging for persistence but uncertain for causal replication.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not label open-label OLE as independent Phase3 replication; cannot claim durable controlled superiority after crossover, full survival benefit, or FDA probability based on this one result.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted exact-NCT conference abstract review of 2026 O33 and comparison to 2025 peer-reviewed primary randomized ENERGIZE trial; a provisional 50/100 MIXED_EVIDENCE research band reflects observed exploratory durability with unresolved causal replication. No independent human adjudication or approval probability.

records.benchmarkId: ABTECT maintenance within-trial placebo response and published UC maintenance benchmark
records.benchmarkContext: The prospective randomized ABTECT-Maintenance control is 20/192 (10.4%) Week-44 clinical remission; both active arms exceeded placebo by about 39–40 percentage points. Published TRUE NORTH ozanimod maintenance trial had 37.0% versus 18.5% (18.5 percentage points). This published cross-program context is NOT a head-to-head benchmark; differences in patient selection and trial timing prevent any claim of therapeutic superiority.
records.observedResult: On the 580-patient randomized double-blind ABTECT-Maintenance exact-trial Phase 3 readout, Week-44 clinical remission occurred in 98/193 (50.8%) at 25mg and 100/195 (51.3%) at 50mg versus 20/192 (10.4%) placebo. Sponsor reports stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 percentage points with both p<0.0001. Observed current results, not predictions.
records.uncertaintyReview: The readout is issuer-reported (SEC-filed), detailed prespecified effect confidence intervals, full SAP, ascertainment, and handling of missing data are not fully independently verified. Patients were induction responders re-randomized for maintenance; this is not efficacy in all initiating patients. Cross-program comparator is contextual only.
records.criticalRiskReview: Strong within-trial placebo-adjusted remission does not establish FDA approval or superior efficacy against other UC drugs. Missing full trial report and adverse-event stratification remain material to overall benefit-risk.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted, exact-NCT review of June 2026 SEC-hosted randomized maintenance endpoint tables against the placebo arm and separately published randomized UC maintenance context. Provisional 75/100 clinical efficacy research band, not calibrated approval or investment probability.

records.benchmarkId: Week-44 patient-important clinical, endoscopic and steroid-free remission versus control
records.benchmarkContext: Clinically meaningful UC benefit is defined using validated clinical remission, endoscopic healing and corticosteroid-free remission rather than p-values alone. The published GEMINI 1 randomized maintenance study used clinical remission and mucosal healing as relevant patient-oriented disease-control endpoints. Different programs and populations cannot establish relative drug ranking.
records.observedResult: At ABTECT-Maintenance Week 44, endoscopic remission was 41.5% (25mg) and 47.7% (50mg) versus placebo 9.9%; corticosteroid-free clinical remission was 45.1% and 47.7% versus 9.9%; sustained clinical remission among remission-at-induction subgroups was 67.1% and 65.6% versus 15.7%. All reported p<0.0001 in issuer SEC exhibit.
records.uncertaintyReview: These are clinically meaningful mucosal and steroid-free measurements, but original public topline lacks complete patient-reported quality-of-life score tables, full multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals and adjudicated missing-data analyses. Sustained remission compares selected induction remitters.
records.criticalRiskReview: Patient-reported symptoms and long-term function cannot be presumed from endoscopy alone; steroid-free benefit and sustained responses should be checked in full CSR and label. Histologic definitions and protocol changes may matter.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted clinical-benefit rubric review comparing within-study clinical/endoscopic/steroid-free arm outcomes to established UC maintenance endpoint precedents. Provisional 75/100 research grade; not a superiority or regulatory forecast.

records.benchmarkId: UC randomized maintenance design, stratified primary effect and statistical sensitivity evidence
records.benchmarkContext: TRUE NORTH reported randomized maintenance remission comparisons and prespecified hierarchical outcomes. The ABTECT 6-K reports adjusted risk differences using Mantel-Haenszel stratification (baseline remission, induction dose and corticosteroid use) with nominal reported p<0.0001 across primary and key secondary endpoints. This is encouraging but does not disclose all analytic details needed to independently test multiplicitiy and missing-data sensitivity.
records.observedResult: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 initial induction responders (placebo 192, 25mg 193, 50mg 195), reporting Week-44 clinical remission 10.4%, 50.8% and 51.3% with stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 points, both p<0.0001; multiplicity and conservative missing-outcome scenarios are not supplied in full SEC summary.
records.uncertaintyReview: Reported p-values and predeclared stratification are not substitutes for accessible final SAP, confidence intervals for all contrasts, imputation, sensitivity analyses or an independently reanalysed dataset. Applicant-controlled topline is the source, so robustness is not fully established.
records.criticalRiskReview: Risk of overconfidence from exceptionally small p-values, responder re-randomization, incomplete ascertainment details, unverified estimand changes or imperfect multiple-comparison adjustment. Missing information is not imputed as an adverse result.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted review of SEC-hosted clinical table and published maintenance-control statistical norms; MIXED_EVIDENCE 50/100 reflects credible randomization and large signals but incomplete independent statistical audit, not grade of an undisclosed SAP.

records.benchmarkId: ABTECT-1 and ABTECT-2 independent induction studies versus ABTECT maintenance duration
records.benchmarkContext: Prior ABTECT-1 and ABTECT-2 randomized induction datasets met their Week-8 clinical-remission primary endpoint for the 50mg arms (ABTECT-1 21.7% vs 2.5% placebo, ABTECT-2 19.8% vs 6.3%). ABTECT-2 25mg clinical-remission contrast was not significant (p=0.1034). These are two distinct induction trials but NOT randomized replication of Week-44 maintenance.
records.observedResult: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 induction responders across 25mg, 50mg and placebo and found Week-44 clinical remission near 51% in both doses versus 10.4% placebo. Sponsor also reports sustained clinical remission among Week-8 remission subgroups 67.1% and 65.6% vs 15.7% placebo. Separate prior induction trials demonstrated consistent 50mg benefit; 25mg induction was less consistent.
records.uncertaintyReview: Maintenance durability is measured in a selected responder population; the maintenance phase itself has no separate blinded confirmatory maintenance study in these sources. Induction and maintenance outcomes involve different populations/endpoints. Long-term 7-year extension described by sponsor is uncontrolled and not independent replication.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not treat open-label multiyear exposure as independent controlled confirmation or infer durable benefit for induction nonresponders. Full retention, dropout handling, prespecified subgroup interaction tests and maintenance replication remain unresolved.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted comparison of the June 2026 maintenance SEC readout with July 2025 ABTECT-1/2 randomized induction tables. Assign 50/100 MIXED_EVIDENCE for duration and repeated program activity but incomplete independent maintenance replication; not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: Within-study arm safety and prior UC maintenance tolerability context
records.benchmarkContext: TRUE NORTH maintenance reported infection rates higher with ozanimod than placebo but serious infection under 2%, furnishing an illustrative UC maintenance treatment setting, not direct head-to-head safety comparison. ABTECT's own placebo arm is primary safety comparator for treatment-emergent events and discontinuations.
records.observedResult: SEC-hosted ABTECT-Maintenance arm table (placebo n192, 25mg n193, 50mg n195): any TEAE 50.0%,58.0%,71.8%; serious TEAE 4.2%,2.6%,5.6%; study-drug discontinuations due to TEAE 6.8%,2.6%,4.6%; deaths 0 all groups. Serious/severe infection events reported 1.0%,1.0%,0.5%. Non-melanoma skin cancers 1 in placebo and 3 each in 25/50mg arms; single cases of prostate, breast and dysplasia in 50mg with attribution uncertain.
records.uncertaintyReview: Dose-related increase in any TEAE (50mg 71.8% vs placebo 50%) counters a uniformly favorable safety claim. Serious event counts are small and uncommon outcomes underpowered; trial selection limits generalizability. Attribution of skin cancers and longer exposure risk not established by topline.
records.criticalRiskReview: Higher 50mg adverse-event burden, rare malignancy imbalances, opportunistic-infection potential and unknown long-term class-specific risks require ongoing surveillance and full safety tables. Do not assume regulatory safety acceptability from 'no new signals' press statement.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted arm-by-arm benefit-risk review of SEC-reported randomized 44-week safety tables with independently published maintenance-therapy context. 50/100 MIXED_EVIDENCE due tolerability imbalance and uncertainty, not absence of safety data.

records.benchmarkId: ROSELLA exact-trial survival and safety post-1-1 reference context
records.benchmarkContext: The original peer-reviewed randomized ROSELLA trial independently documents blinded central PFS review and active nab-paclitaxel monotherapy control.
records.observedResult: FDA ROSELLA randomized n381: PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.91), p=0.0076; OS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83), p=0.0004, median OS 16.0 vs 11.9 months.
records.uncertaintyReview: Open-label design and differing doses of nab-paclitaxel in the treatment arms limit direct attribution; no independent pivotal replication is claimed.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not apply the observed survival result outside the specific prior-bevacizumab 1-3-line population or assume an efficacy grade proves a stock return.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted independent-source comparison of FDA approval summary and peer-reviewed ROSELLA survival, with explicit limitations; provisional ordinal clinical research grade, not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: ROSELLA exact-trial survival and safety post-1-2 reference context
records.benchmarkContext: FDA independently confirmed a 4.1-month observed median survival gain and significant PFS in the randomized platinum-resistant ovarian cancer population.
records.observedResult: At median 24.8 months follow-up, final ROSELLA OS was 16.0 versus 11.9 months, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83), p=0.0004; survival at 18 months 46% combination versus 27% monotherapy.
records.uncertaintyReview: Quality-of-life, symptoms and subjective patient-reported benefit are not established solely by statistically significant all-cause survival; strict entry criteria matter.
records.criticalRiskReview: Survival benefit may not translate into improved daily function for every person; treatment toxicities and contraindications can offset benefits.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted independent-source comparison of FDA approval summary and peer-reviewed ROSELLA survival, with explicit limitations; provisional ordinal clinical research grade, not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: ROSELLA exact-trial survival and safety post-1-3 reference context
records.benchmarkContext: Prespecified survival endpoints, blinded-independent central PFS review and a mature peer-reviewed final OS report offer stronger statistical evidence than a sponsor topline.
records.observedResult: FDA summary reports two-sided PFS p=0.0076 HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.91) and OS p=0.0004 HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83) from the randomized 381-patient trial.
records.uncertaintyReview: Public summary does not detail all missing-data rules, multiplicity allocation, censoring sensitivities or treatment-arm dose impact; not a reanalysis of individual patient data.
records.criticalRiskReview: Open-label design and chemotherapy dose imbalance warrant continued sensitivity review despite FDA acceptance of efficacy.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted independent-source comparison of FDA approval summary and peer-reviewed ROSELLA survival, with explicit limitations; provisional ordinal clinical research grade, not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: ROSELLA exact-trial survival and safety post-1-4 reference context
records.benchmarkContext: Earlier peer-reviewed ROSELLA PFS and interim OS results provide a temporal comparator for mature survival, but both analyses use the same pivotal randomized participants.
records.observedResult: Final ROSELLA overall-survival HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.83) after median 24.8-month follow-up was consistent with same-trial earlier interim OS HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.52-0.92).
records.uncertaintyReview: A longer follow-up on the same trial is not independent randomized replication, and subgroup interactions remain uncertain.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not count repeated analyses of one cohort as distinct confirmatory Phase 3 trials or generalize to excluded populations.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted independent-source comparison of FDA approval summary and peer-reviewed ROSELLA survival, with explicit limitations; provisional ordinal clinical research grade, not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: ROSELLA exact-trial survival and safety post-1-5 reference context
records.benchmarkContext: FDA labeled benefits and serious risks supply an independent benefit-risk context, alongside peer-reviewed mature ROSELLA exposure-adjusted safety observations.
records.observedResult: FDA approval includes warnings for neutropenia/severe infections, adrenal insufficiency and embryo-fetal toxicity and contraindication for lifesaving steroid requirements. Final Lancet reports neutropenia 64%, anemia 61%, fatigue 54% and nausea 44% in combination patients.
records.uncertaintyReview: Differential exposure duration and nab-paclitaxel dosage make simple cross-arm safety-event comparisons imperfect; rare risks and postmarketing data remain limited.
records.criticalRiskReview: FDA approval is not absence of toxicity; clinical safety depends on infection risk, neutropenia and the need for corticosteroids.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted independent-source comparison of FDA approval summary and peer-reviewed ROSELLA survival, with explicit limitations; provisional ordinal clinical research grade, not FDA probability.

records.benchmarkId: ENERGIZE-T exact-NCT primary randomized 48-week versus ongoing five-year extension review
records.benchmarkContext: The September 2026 clinical-trials review confirms a 48-week randomized 2:1 ENERGIZE-T transfusion-reduction study and a planned open-label extension lasting up to five years. Transfusion-reduction response is achieved in ANY consecutive 12-week period, not proof of continuous benefit throughout 48 weeks. Independent placebo-controlled replication or post-extension causal durability is not established by this report.
records.observedResult: In peer-reviewed randomized ENERGIZE-T, 238 of 258 (92%) randomized participants completed the double-blind period. At least one qualifying 12-week transfusion-reduction response occurred in 52/171 (30%) mitapivat vs 11/87 (13%) placebo; adjusted difference 18 percentage points (95% CI 8–27), p=0.0003. Its long open-label extension continues and cannot be used as blinded durability replication.
records.uncertaintyReview: The primary 'any 12-week window' response does not establish sustained reduction for each participant across the entire 48-week period. Longer-term observational extension participants are selected and receive no concurrent placebo; results, attrition patterns and long-horizon response trajectories remain incompletely disclosed.
records.criticalRiskReview: Do not label 48-week study duration as 48-week continuous efficacy, or call the nonrandomized planned OLE independent confirmatory trial evidence. Hemoglobin benefit and durability may vary by thalassemia genotype and baseline transfusion burden.
records.reviewerMethod: AI-assisted review of dated peer-reviewed Lancet exact-NCT controlled ENERGIZE-T results and 2026 American Journal of Hematology trial-status context. MIXED_EVIDENCE 50/100 is provisional clinical durability and replication assessment, not FDA approval or market probability.
